corrected_proposal.description_short: CNN reported an April 10 internal plan proposed a CDC budget reduction of more than 40%; the draft could change and was not an enacted cut.

corrected_proposal.description_long: CNN reported on April 16, 2025, that an internal Trump administration document dated April 10 outlined a proposed reduction of more than 40% in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s budget. The document also previewed a broader restructuring of federal health agencies and consolidation of programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. CNN reported that the plan could still be finalized with changes and described the reductions as what would happen “if enacted as is.” The evidence supports a proposed budget action; it does not show that the CDC had already received a 40% reduction in March. Nor does the accessed reporting substantiate that every program named in the original synopsis—including outbreak-detection grants, chronic-disease programs, global surveillance across 49 countries, and state emergency-preparedness agreements—was eliminated by this same proposal. This card therefore focuses on the April 10 proposal and leaves implementation unresolved. It does not combine the proposal, agency layoffs, and program closures into one completed event. The percentage is CNN’s description of the administration’s plan, not a final appropriation or an independently audited spending change.

corrected_proposal.description_medium: The supplied record alleges that Trump posted on February 15, 2025, threatening universities' tax-exempt status over DEI, protest policies, and faculty governance. The packet supplies no matching post or source excerpt. Separate February reporting concerns an Education Department funding warning over DEI, while later reporting concerns Harvard specifically. Neither establishes the supplied February tax-status claim, so this remains an internal, unverified draft.
corrected_proposal.description_long: The supplied card alleges that Donald Trump posted on February 15, 2025, threatening to revoke the tax-exempt status of universities that rejected administration demands concerning DEI, campus protest policies, and faculty governance. The packet contains no original post URL or source excerpt establishing that date, broad university scope, or the stated conditions. Search excerpts surfaced separate February reporting about an Education Department warning that institutions could lose federal funding over DEI, and April reporting about a Harvard-specific tax-status threat. Those reports concern different actions, dates, and scopes; they do not verify this allegation and are not substituted as the event. The supplied text also asserts that endowments worth tens of billions of dollars could be exposed, that research programs faced severe consequences, that legal scholars identified First Amendment problems, that university boards held emergency reviews, and that the threat sent shockwaves through higher education. The packet supplies no supporting excerpts for those details. The alleged February date, broad university scope, and conditions therefore remain unverified.
